scores.claim_text: Independent testing laboratory confirmed in December 2025 that the AI-1 smartphone battery delivered volumetric energy density of 935 Wh/L (+12% vs leading silicon-doped commercial smartphone battery).
scores.M_check: Patent-portfolio depth proxy + battery-specific Heuristic 9 (energy-density without test conditions).
scores.interpretation: Patent depth (61 granted, mostly battery/electrode/cell, 7 silicon-anode in title) is fully consistent with a real silicon-anode platform company — PASS on patent corroboration. However the 935 Wh/L claim is reported WITHOUT test conditions (rate, temperature, depth-of-discharge) in the 10-K business section, despite Heuristic 9's explicit requirement. Comparison anchor ('leading silicon-doped commercially available battery tested by 12%') is unnamed. Independent-lab attestation is asserted but the lab is not identified. This is a disclosure-quality issue for what is the central technology marketing number, so MODERATE per Heuristic 9. Not SEVERE because conditions aren't actively contradicted elsewhere and the patent base supports the underlying architecture story.

scores.claim_text: Cell architecture designed to enable silicon anodes to achieve >=1,000 cycles to 80% remaining capacity.
scores.M_check: Reuse of patent corroboration + Heuristic 9 (test-condition disclosure).
scores.interpretation: Cycle-life number is also given without rate / DoD / temperature qualifications and is explicitly framed as a DESIGN TARGET ('designed to enable') rather than a measured value on AI-1 production cells. Smartphone applications typically test at 0.5C-1C with shallow DoD, where 1000 cycles is industry-baseline (not a differentiator). MODERATE due to unconditional framing and design-target hedge. The architecture itself is patent-supported — not SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Partnered with a top-tier mobile OEM (unnamed) on AI-1 smartphone battery; delivered 1,000+ AI-1 packs to lead smart-eyewear customer + samples to 9 OEMs/ODMs.
scores.M_check: Heuristic 7 counterparty-disclosure threshold + Heuristic 6 name-variant + Heuristic 3 stage-ladder.

M_value.note: 411 universe hits appear dominated by Enovix's own filings

scores.interpretation: The mobile OEM is UNNAMED — the framework cannot do a counterparty-disclosure cross-check. Apple's filings contain ZERO mentions of Enovix as of cutoff, but Apple does not disclose suppliers individually so absence is not dispositive (UNVERIFIABLE for any specific OEM). On the stage ladder, 'partnered on development' is a JDA-equivalent, not a design-win for series production; the 1,000+ eyewear packs is real product shipment but to one lead customer + 9 ODMs is still sample-stage breadth. Performance obligations on the balance sheet are only $5.3M, supporting that no series-production OEM contract has been booked. MODERATE: the technology engagement is real but the disclosure conflates JDA / sample-shipment with future commercial revenue. Not SEVERE because production-line shipments to a named-lead eyewear customer ARE happening.

scores.claim_text: Fab2 Penang Malaysia operational with 3 lines (Pilot, Agility, HVM); Agility shipping cells since Oct 2024; SAT complete YE-2024.
scores.M_check: Heuristic 1 EPA FRS scope (Malaysian site is not in EPA FRS) + Heuristic 2 foreign-issuer caveat.

M_value.reason: Fab2 is in Malaysia; EPA FRS only covers US facilities

scores.interpretation: Fab2 is in Malaysia and therefore outside EPA FRS scope — no independent US-regulator corroboration available. The facility is repeatedly referenced across Enovix's own 8-K and 10-K filings (25 hits) which is consistent with continuous disclosure cadence (groundbreaking, opening ceremony, ISO 9001 audit). No counterparty filing independently confirms operational status. The 2023 securities class action (C8) explicitly concerns prior statements about manufacturing scale-up, which raises sensitivity around this category of claim. UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS because the framework's primary corroboration sources (EPA FRS, US-counterparty filings) don't reach a Penang facility.

scores.claim_text: Acquired Routejade (Korea) in 2023 and adjacent SolarEdge-Korean facility in 2025; total Korea footprint 467,400 sqft owned.
scores.M_check: Heuristic 2 foreign-issuer caveat (Korean facility) + filing-cadence corroboration.
scores.interpretation: Routejade is a real prior-existing Korean battery manufacturer, consistently disclosed across Enovix's 10-K/10-Q/8-K since the 2023 acquisition (28 hits, all from Enovix). The transaction was specifically disclosed with a Stock Purchase Agreement filed Sep 2023. Property table claims 467,400 sqft owned in Korea, consistent with a real production base + 2025 expansion. PASS because (a) acquisition has been in the financials for 3 fiscal years with no claw-back; (b) defense/industrial revenue is being recognized through Korean entities; (c) no contradiction available from any source.

scores.claim_text: Defense and industrial markets growing through Korea operations: drones, subsea systems, munitions.
scores.M_check: USAspending direct DoD contract search (Heuristic 5 source-jurisdiction mismatch — cell suppliers usually sell to system primes, not DoD direct).
scores.interpretation: Zero direct federal contracts for Enovix or Routejade. Battery cell suppliers typically sell to drone/munitions primes (Anduril, AeroVironment, Red Cat, Kratos, etc.) not directly to DoD, so absence is not a hard contradiction per Heuristic 5. However, the framework cannot independently corroborate the 'increased shipments' / growing-defense-business claim — there are no named end-customers, no quantified contract values, no public defense-prime corroboration. UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED because (i) Korean defense customers wouldn't appear in USAspending and (ii) commercial cell sales to drone primes wouldn't either. Not PASS because the claim is uncorroborated by any independent source.

scores.claim_text: Distress markers: accumulated deficit $977.8M, working capital $477.2M, $60M buyback FY25, additional $75M subsequent buyback authorized, 2028 (3.00%) + 2030 (4.75%) Convertibles, ATM, warrant dividend issued July 2025 and early-expired August 2025.
scores.M_check: Heuristic 10 (delisting / going-concern fingerprints) + Heuristic 4 (investment vs operating).
scores.interpretation: Mixed signals. Going-concern language is present BUT the company has $477M working capital and is buying back its own shares — that is INCONSISTENT with classic Heuristic 10 distress fingerprint, suggesting more solvency than a typical SPAC-era battery name. However, the simultaneous mix is unusual: convertible debt at 4.75% (2030 issuance), ATM open, buyback executed near 52-week-low prices (avg $10.74), warrant dividend issued AND early-expired within 6 weeks — these are classic stock-price-management mechanics. Repeated capital-structure churn (Affiliate Notes from Chairman, warrant dividend tied to 30-day VWAP $10.50 condition) is a yellow-flag for managing optics of a stalled commercial ramp. Cumulative deficit ~$978M against effectively pre-revenue commercial ramp (performance obligations only $5.3M) signals burn vs commercial-traction gap. MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: Securities class action (N.D. Cal. 23-cv-00071-SI) alleges material misstatements about manufacturing scale-up / equipment testing; one statement remains active after Oct 2025 partial dismissal; class cert hearing March 2026.
scores.M_check: Direct filing disclosure; cross-reference to category of current claims (C1 / C2 / C4 are all in the same lineage — manufacturing & technology performance statements).
scores.interpretation: Active securities-fraud case targeting the EXACT category of claims the framework is scoring (manufacturing scale-up, equipment testing). One statement survived motion practice and is proceeding to class certification. The 10-K's own forward statements about Fab2 ramp (C4), AI-1 testing (C1), and cycle-life targets (C2) are in the same lineage as the litigated statements. The case is not a death-knell — partial dismissal granted Jul 2024 and Oct 2025 dismissed 2 of 3 surviving statements — but it elevates scrutiny on technology / manufacturing claims. MODERATE: a settled or dismissed case would be PASS; an in-progress case with surviving claims at class-cert stage on the same claim-category is a real signal but not catastrophic.
